final_answer:
Merge sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm that works by recursively dividing the input into two halves, sorting each half, and then merging them back together to form a single sorted list. The merge process combines two sorted arrays into one sorted array. This ensures a time complexity of O(n log n), and the algorithm is stable, preserving the relative order of equal elements.

Merge sort is preferred over quicksort for linked lists because quicksort requires random access to elements, which is inefficient for linked lists due to their sequential access nature. Merge sort works well with sequential access and avoids the overhead of partitioning in quicksort. It is also more suitable for linked lists due to its structure and memory-efficient handling of sequential data.
